title: Combining in situ SEM and TEM Deformation with HREBSD Analysis to Understand Dislocation/Grain Boundary Interactions – From Unit Processes to Resolved Stress Fields
content: Dislocation/grain boundary interactions dictate much of the deformation and failure processes in structural materials, from determining the strength of polycrystalline materials to driving fatigue crack initiation processes. In situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has been used for decades to provide insight into the unit processes accompanying these interactions, but typically only provide qualitative information on the stress state [1, 2]. High resolution electron backscatter diffraction (HREBSD) provides access to the elastic strain and stress state of the material [3], but is typically applied under static or relaxed conditions where the stress fields are often different than what they were under loaded conditions. In this study, we combine insights from in situ TEM deformation experiments with in situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM)/HREBSD experiments to understand what factors govern the barrier strength to dislocation glide in polycrystalline materials.
